_transcription: ENGLISH PAGES = the EVEN 0-based indices 2, 4 and 6. All EIGHT rendered indices were opened and accounted for, not just the even ones. PAGE MAP: idx 0 cover (Series ABCD5/5, SET No. 3, Q.P. Code 65/5/3, bilingual, 'contains 7 printed pages', 'contains 14 questions', 2 hours / 40 marks); idx 1 HINDI General Instructions (सामान्य निर्देश) + Hindi Q1-Q4; idx 2 ENGLISH General Instructions + SECTION A Q1-Q4; idx 3 HINDI Q5-Q6 + Hindi खण्ड ख Q7-Q10; idx 4 ENGLISH Q5-Q6 + SECTION B Q7-Q10; idx 5 HINDI खण्ड ग Q11-Q14; idx 6 ENGLISH SECTION C Q11-Q14; idx 7 BLANK apart from the QR code and the '65/5/3 8' footer. Started from out/2022-65-5-3/contact.png as the brief now directs — the idx-labelled thumbnail grid settled the language of all eight pages in a single Read — then confirmed every load-bearing reading against the full-size page. THE ALTERNATION HYPOTHESIS HELD, and it was CHECKED rather than assumed: a composite of the TOP 520px of all four odd indices (1, 3, 5, 7) was rendered and read, and every one of them is Hindi or blank, so there is NO English overflow onto any odd page and NO mid-paper parity inversion of the kind the brief records for 2026 65/3/3. The three failure modes the brief warns about are therefore all absent here — a checked absence, not an assumed one. ONE THING THAT LOOKS LIKE ENGLISH ON AN ODD PAGE AND IS NOT: idx 7 carries a faint MIRRORED ghost of idx 6's English SECTION C. It is scanner show-through from the reverse of the sheet, reversed left-to-right and legible only as a mirror image; it is not content and nothing was taken from it. Question numbers run 1-14 unbroken with every sub-part present, and each language block runs a whole page, so the English Q4->Q5 and Q10->Q11 hand-offs jump the intervening Hindi page cleanly. FOLIO/COVER MISMATCH, the same class the brief records for 2026 65/3/1 and the reference paper records for 65/5/1: the cover says 7 printed pages, the last English folio (idx 6) reads 7, and idx 7 is a blank eighth page whose footer reads 8. INTERNAL CHOICE = FOUR (Q3, Q7, Q8, Q12). Instruction (vi) prints NO count ('There is an internal choice in some questions.'), so per the brief this was established by walking the OFFICIAL MARKING SCHEME question by question across all ten ms pages — it reprints each question block and then both branches under 'Or': Q3 has A3.(a)/A3.(b) [ms idx 2-3], Q7 has A7.(a)/A7.(b) [ms idx 4-5], Q8 has A8.(a)/A8.(b) [ms idx 5-6], Q12 has A12.(a)/A12.(b) [ms idx 7-8]. Q1, Q2, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q9, Q10, Q11, Q13 and Q14 each have a single answer block with no 'Or' — again a checked absence. Q14 is NOT an internal choice: its (a) and (b) are genuine SUB-PARTS of 2 marks each and the scheme marks BOTH (A14.(a) and A14.(b), no 'Or' between them), matching printed instruction (7), 'Question 14 is a case study based question with two subparts of 2 marks each.' Cross-check on marks: primary branches 6x2 = 12 in A, 4x3 = 12 in B, 3x4 + (2+2) = 16 in C, total 40, matching the cover — but per the brief that sum is structurally blind to a MISSED alternative, which is why the count rests on the scheme walk and not on the sum. NO MCQs ANYWHERE, confirmed on both English question pages and throughout the marking scheme: all 14 questions are free-response, so every row is 'subjective', no row carries options or an 'answer', and the blind MCQ key re-derivation that anchors 2023-2026 cannot run on this paper at all. Decimal points: this paper prints NO decimal numbers at all — unlike 65/5/1, whose Q11 prints 0.8/0.5/0.3 — so the raised-dot question ({\cdot}) does not arise on any row here. OVERLAP WITH 65/5/1, MEASURED BY CONTENT AND NOT BY plan.txt: 15 of the 19 rows are the same printed block as the reference paper, reshuffled and renumbered, and 4 are NEW. The shared 15, in this paper's numbering -> the reference's: Q2->Q1, Q3a->Q6a, Q3b->Q6b, Q4->Q2, Q5->Q4, Q6->Q3, Q7a->Q8a, Q7b->Q8b, Q8a->Q10a, Q8b->Q10b, Q11->Q12, Q12a->Q13a, Q12b->Q13b, Q14a->Q14a, Q14b->Q14b. Each was read on MY page first and only then given the reference's stem/context text byte-for-byte, which is the brief's recommended method: the full sitting is reconstructable from this file and the duplicate rows still collapse on content_hash at commit. The 4 genuinely NEW questions are Q1 (Cartesian equation of line AB, direction cosines of a parallel line), Q9 (the King's-rule definite integral from 1 to 3), Q10 (distance of a point measured along a line from a plane) and Q13 (two-box Bayes). plan.txt WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, exactly as the brief predicts. It indexes only 13 blocks against this paper's 19 rows, and its block->number attributions do not survive a content check: it claims 'Q2#1 = 65-5-1 Q4#2' when this paper's Q2 is the reference's Q1, and 'Q4#1 = 65-5-1 Q1#1' when this paper's Q4 is the reference's Q2. It named Q10 and Q13 as new, which content confirms — but it is silent on Q1 and Q9, which are also new and appear in neither of its lists. Nothing was skipped on the strength of the file; all 19 rows are transcribed. NO solutions written for any row, per the brief. TWO ITEMS FOR THE NEXT AGENT. (1) Q3(a) is the SAME CBSE defect the reference paper flags on its Q6(a) — three mutually inconsistent probabilities — and it is reproduced here verbatim, question and marking scheme alike; see the _flag on Q3a, which records the 5x crop of the printed bars and the scheme's own uncorrected working. It should now be expected on every set of the 65/5 series. (2) Q10 asks for a distance measured from a PLANE, so it is filed on the 'The Plane' subtopic added to the live axis on 2026-08-19 for exactly this pre-rationalisation paper; no flag is raised, per the brief. It is the ONLY plane question here — Q1 is direction cosines and Q14 (a)/(b) are both about the two given LINES (shortest distance, then their point of intersection), so neither belongs there. ALSO NOTED, affecting no row and raised as no flag: (i) Q10's point (2, 3, 4) does NOT lie on the given line — (2-4)/3, (3+5)/6 and (4+1)/2 are -2/3, 4/3 and 5/2 — so 'measured along the line' means measured PARALLEL to it, which is how CBSE's own scheme reads it (A10 opens 'Equation of line through (2, 3, 4) and parallel to the given line'), giving the foot (-1, -3, 2) and distance 7. The question is well posed; this is recorded only so a later author does not mistake it for a point-on-line problem. (ii) The marking scheme's A1 confirms the intended reading of Q1's leading coefficient: it normalises (2x-1)/12 to (x - 1/2)/6 and reports direction ratios 6, 2, 3 and direction cosines (6/7, 2/7, 3/7).

questions.stem:
The Cartesian equation of a line AB is :

\(\dfrac{2x - 1}{12} = \dfrac{y + 2}{2} = \dfrac{z - 3}{3}\)

Find the direction cosines of a line parallel to line AB.

Events A and B are such that

\(P(A) = \dfrac{1}{2}\), \(P(B) = \dfrac{7}{12}\) and \(P\left(\overline{A} \cup \overline{B}\right) = \dfrac{1}{4}\)

Find whether the events A and B are independent or not.
questions._flag: CBSE DEFECT — the three given probabilities are MUTUALLY INCONSISTENT. Verified on a 5x crop of page idx 2: the bars are printed over A and over B SEPARATELY (two distinct bars with a clear gap at the union sign), so the given quantity is \(P(\overline{A} \cup \overline{B})\) and De Morgan gives \(P(A \cap B) = 1 - 1/4 = 3/4\) — which exceeds \(P(A) = 1/2\) and is therefore impossible for any pair of events. The official marking scheme reproduces the same separate bars and performs exactly that step (ms idx 3, A3.(a) writes \(P(\overline{A} \cup \overline{B}) = P(\overline{A \cap B}) = 1 - P(A \cap B)\), then \(P(A \cap B) = 1 - 1/4 = 3/4\)) and does NOT notice the contradiction; it concludes 'A and B are not independent' by comparing 3/4 against \(P(A) \times P(B) = 7/24\). Transcribed exactly as printed. Note the reading \(P(\overline{A \cup B}) = 1/4\) — a single bar spanning the union — would be consistent (it gives \(P(A \cap B) = 1/3 \ne 7/24\), same verdict), but that is NOT what either document prints and it is not adopted here. This is the SAME block, defect included, that the reference paper 65/5/1 carries as its Q6(a); expect it across the 65/5 series.

questions.stem: A box \(B_1\) contains 1 white ball and 3 red balls. Another box \(B_2\) contains 2 white balls and 3 red balls. If one ball is drawn at random from each of the boxes \(B_1\) and \(B_2\), then find the probability that the two balls drawn are of the same colour.

Find the general solution of the following differential equation :

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{x-y} + x^2 e^{-y}\)

Let X be a random variable which assumes values \(x_1\), \(x_2\), \(x_3\), \(x_4\) such that \(2P(X = x_1) = 3P(X = x_2) = P(X = x_3) = 5P(X = x_4)\).

Find the probability distribution of X.

If \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) are two vectors such that \(\left|\vec{a} + \vec{b}\right| = \left|\vec{b}\right|\), then prove that \(\left(\vec{a} + 2\vec{b}\right)\) is perpendicular to \(\vec{a}\).

If \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) are unit vectors and \(\theta\) is the angle between them, then prove that

\(\sin \dfrac{\theta}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left|\vec{a} - \vec{b}\right|\).
Find the distance of the point \((2, 3, 4)\) measured along the line \(\dfrac{x - 4}{3} = \dfrac{y + 5}{6} = \dfrac{z + 1}{2}\) from the plane \(3x + 2y + 2z + 5 = 0\).

questions.subtopic: Area Bounded by a Curve and a Line
questions.stem: Find the area bounded by the curves \(y = |x - 1|\) and \(y = 1\), using integration.

Solve the following differential equation :

\(\left(y - \sin^2 x\right) dx + \tan x\, dy = 0\)

Find the general solution of the differential equation :

\(\left(x^3 + y^3\right) dy = x^2 y\, dx\)

There are two boxes, namely box-I and box-II. Box-I contains 3 red and 6 black balls. Box-II contains 5 red and 5 black balls. One of the two boxes, is selected at random and a ball is drawn at random. The ball drawn is found to be red. Find the probability that this red ball comes out from box-II.
questions._flag: PRINTING SLIP, transcribed AS PRINTED and not answer-affecting: the stem carries a stray comma in 'One of the two boxes, is selected at random'. Verified on a 3x crop of page idx 6 — the comma is genuinely on the page and is not a transcription artefact. The official marking scheme (ms idx 8) reprints the question with the same stray comma. Recorded so a later reader does not 'repair' it and change content_hash.
